rows.question: For each building type, list the name of the building type, the number of buildings that are not subdivisions, number of employees, number of unique building street address, number of unique city, number of unique state, number of unique postal code, and average gross square footage per employee. For building type of 'resident', display it as 'RESIDENTIAL'. Include a grand total across all building types (the corresponding type field is 'TOTAL').
rows.pred_sql:
WITH buildings_norm AS (
  SELECT
    BUILDING_KEY,
    BUILDING_NUMBER,
    BUILDING_NAME,
    BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS,
    BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS,
    BUILDING_TYPE,
    COALESCE(BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,0) AS BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
    COALESCE(BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,0) AS BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
    COALESCE(BUILDING_COUNTER,0) AS BUILDING_COUNTER,
    WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
  FROM buildings
),
building_addresses AS (
  SELECT
    fba.BUILDING_KEY,
    fba.STREET_NUMBER,
    fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL,
    fba.STREET_NAME,
    fba.STREET_SUFFIX,
    fba.POST_DIRECTIONAL,
    fba.CITY,
    fba.STATE,
    fba.POSTAL_CODE,
    TRIM(
      CONCAT_WS(' ',
        NULLIF(fba.STREET_NUMBER,''),
        NULLIF(fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL,''),
        NULLIF(fba.STREET_NAME,''),
        NULLIF(fba.STREET_SUFFIX,''),
        NULLIF(fba.POST_DIRECTIONAL,'')
      )
    ) AS street_addr,
    fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE
  FROM fac_building_address fba
  WHERE fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE = 'STREET'
),
employee_by_building_number AS (
  SELECT
    OFFICE_LOCATION AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
    COUNT(*) AS emp_count
  FROM employee_directory
  WHERE OFFICE_LOCATION IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(OFFICE_LOCATION) <> ''
  GROUP BY OFFICE_LOCATION
),
building_employees AS (
  SELECT
    bn.BUILDING_KEY,
    COALESCE(ebbn.emp_count,0) AS emp_count
  FROM buildings_norm bn
  LEFT JOIN employee_by_building_number ebbn
    ON ebbn.BUILDING_NUMBER = bn.BUILDING_NUMBER
),
building_addr_norm AS (
  SELECT
    bn.BUILDING_KEY,
    CASE
      WHEN TRIM(COALESCE(bn.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS,'')) <> '' THEN TRIM(bn.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS)
      ELSE TRIM(ba.street_addr)
    END AS STREET_ADDRESS,
    COALESCE(ba.CITY, '') AS CITY,
    COALESCE(ba.STATE, '') AS STATE,
    COALESCE(ba.POSTAL_CODE, '') AS POSTAL_CODE
  FROM buildings_norm bn
  LEFT JOIN building_addresses ba
    ON bn.BUILDING_KEY = ba.BUILDING_KEY
),
per_building AS (
  SELECT
    bn.BUILDING_KEY,
    bn.BUILDING_TYPE,
    CASE
      WHEN UPPER(COALESCE(bn.BUILDING_TYPE,'')) = 'RESIDENT' THEN 'RESIDENTIAL'
      WHEN TRIM(COALESCE(bn.BUILDING_TYPE,'')) = '' THEN 'UNKNOWN'
      ELSE bn.BUILDING_TYPE
    END AS building_type_norm,
    bn.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
    COALESCE(be.emp_count,0) AS emp_count,
    ban.STREET_ADDRESS,
    ban.CITY,
    ban.STATE,
    ban.POSTAL_CODE
  FROM buildings_norm bn
  LEFT JOIN building_employees be ON bn.BUILDING_KEY = be.BUILDING_KEY
  LEFT JOIN building_addr_norm ban ON bn.BUILDING_KEY = ban.BUILDING_KEY
)
SELECT
  building_type_norm AS building_type,
  COUNT(DISTINCT BUILDING_KEY) AS non_subdivision_building_count,
  SUM(emp_count) AS total_employees,
  COUNT(DISTINCT NULLIF(STREET_ADDRESS,'')) AS unique_street_address_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT NULLIF(CITY,'')) AS unique_city_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT NULLIF(STATE,'')) AS unique_state_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT NULLIF(POSTAL_CODE,'')) AS unique_postal_code_count,
  CASE WHEN SUM(emp_count) > 0 THEN ROUND(SUM(BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE)/SUM(emp_count),2) ELSE NULL END AS avg_gross_sqft_per_employee
FROM per_building
GROUP BY building_type_norm

UNION ALL

SELECT
  'TOTAL' AS building_type,
  COUNT(DISTINCT BUILDING_KEY) AS non_subdivision_building_count,
  SUM(emp_count) AS total_employees,
  COUNT(DISTINCT NULLIF(STREET_ADDRESS,'')) AS unique_street_address_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT NULLIF(CITY,'')) AS unique_city_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT NULLIF(STATE,'')) AS unique_state_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT NULLIF(POSTAL_CODE,'')) AS unique_postal_code_count,
  CASE WHEN SUM(emp_count) > 0 THEN ROUND(SUM(BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE)/SUM(emp_count),2) ELSE NULL END AS avg_gross_sqft_per_employee
FROM per_building

rows.question: List each organization's break group, ID, name, and formatted name according to its level, along with whether its members are emeritus or non-emeritus. Also, include the organization number, level, employer count, and hierarchy type for each organization. Exclude organizations '139' and '250'. Sort the results by hierarchy type and ensure totals for employer counts are displayed.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH organization_rowlevel_employees AS (
  -- use faculty roster as the member source (has EMERITUS_STATUS and HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE)
  SELECT
    MIT_ID,
    HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
    EMERITUS_STATUS
  FROM hr_faculty_roster
),
organization_dimension AS (
  -- build organization dimension from fclt_organization (primary) and fallback to fac_organization / sis_department where helpful
  SELECT
    f.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
    COALESCE(f.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME, f.ORGANIZATION_NAME, fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME, s.DEPARTMENT_NAME) AS ORGANIZATION_NAME,
    f.ORGANIZATION_ID,
    f.ORGANIZATION AS ORGANIZATION,
    f.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER,
    f.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL,
    f.DLC_NAME,
    f.DLC_KEY,
    -- BREAK_GROUP not present in schema; derive a simple break grouping from MAJOR_ORG or ORGANIZATION_LEVEL
    COALESCE(f.MAJOR_ORG, fo.MAJOR_ORG, s.SCHOOL_NAME) AS BREAK_GROUP,
    CASE
      WHEN f.DLC_KEY IS NOT NULL THEN 'DLC'
      WHEN s.SCHOOL_CODE IS NOT NULL THEN 'SCHOOL'
      WHEN fo.ORGANIZATION_ID IS NOT NULL THEN 'FAC_ORG'
      ELSE 'OTHER'
    END AS HIERARCHY_TYPE
  FROM fclt_organization f
  LEFT JOIN fac_organization fo ON fo.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID = f.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID
  LEFT JOIN sis_department s ON s.DEPARTMENT_CODE = f.HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD
),
agg_counts AS (
  -- count members per organization (by department code) and emeritus category
  SELECT
    ore.DEPARTMENT_CODE,
    CASE WHEN ore.EMERITUS_STATUS = 'Emeritus' THEN 'Emeritus' ELSE 'Non-Emeritus' END AS EMERITUS_STATUS_CATEGORY,
    COUNT(DISTINCT ore.MIT_ID) AS EMPLOYER_COUNT
  FROM organization_rowlevel_employees ore
  GROUP BY ore.DEPARTMENT_CODE, EMERITUS_STATUS_CATEGORY
),
dept_totals AS (
  -- total employers per department (summing both emeritus categories)
  SELECT
    DEPARTMENT_CODE,
    SUM(EMPLOYER_COUNT) AS TOTAL_EMPLOYER_COUNT
  FROM agg_counts
  GROUP BY DEPARTMENT_CODE
)
SELECT
  od.BREAK_GROUP AS BREAK_GROUP,
  COALESCE(od.ORGANIZATION_ID, od.DEPARTMENT_CODE) AS ORGANIZATION_ID,
  od.ORGANIZATION_NAME AS ORGANIZATION_NAME,
  -- formatted name by level: include level if available
  CASE
    WHEN od.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(od.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL) <> '' THEN CONCAT(od.ORGANIZATION_NAME, ' (Level ', od.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL, ')')
    ELSE od.ORGANIZATION_NAME
  END AS FORMATTED_NAME_BY_LEVEL,
  ac.EMERITUS_STATUS_CATEGORY AS EMERITUS_STATUS_CATEGORY,
  od.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER AS ORGANIZATION_NUMBER,
  od.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL AS LEVEL,
  COALESCE(ac.EMPLOYER_COUNT, 0) AS EMPLOYER_COUNT,
  od.HIERARCHY_TYPE AS HIERARCHY_TYPE,
  COALESCE(dt.TOTAL_EMPLOYER_COUNT, 0) AS TOTAL_EMPLOYER_COUNT
FROM organization_dimension od
LEFT JOIN agg_counts ac
  ON ac.DEPARTMENT_CODE = od.DEPARTMENT_CODE
LEFT JOIN dept_totals dt
  ON dt.DEPARTMENT_CODE = od.DEPARTMENT_CODE
WHERE COALESCE(od.ORGANIZATION_ID, od.DEPARTMENT_CODE) IS NOT NULL
  AND COALESCE(od.ORGANIZATION_ID, od.DEPARTMENT_CODE) NOT IN ('139','250')
ORDER BY od.HIERARCHY_TYPE ASC, COALESCE(od.ORGANIZATION_ID, od.DEPARTMENT_CODE), ac.EMERITUS_STATUS_CATEGORY

rows.question: For each course, list its title, name of the building of the course location, duration (in terms of days), and a running average of the duration (in terms of days) using a window of two preceding and two following courses (partitioned by academic year and sorted by course start date).
rows.pred_sql:
WITH buildings_basic AS (
  SELECT
    `BUILDING_NUMBER` AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
    `BUILDING_NAME` AS BUILDING_NAME
  FROM `buildings`
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(cc.SUBJECT_TITLE, cc.SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE, so.SUBJECT_TITLE) AS course_title,
  bb.BUILDING_NAME AS building_name,
  -- duration in days: end_date - start_date
  DATEDIFF(
    STR_TO_DATE(cd.END_DATE, '%Y-%m-%d'),
    STR_TO_DATE(cd.START_DATE, '%Y-%m-%d')
  ) AS duration_days,
  -- running average over window 2 preceding to 2 following, partitioned by academic year,
  -- ordered by start date with a tie-breaker to make ordering deterministic
  AVG(
    DATEDIFF(
      STR_TO_DATE(cd.END_DATE, '%Y-%m-%d'),
      STR_TO_DATE(cd.START_DATE, '%Y-%m-%d')
    )
  ) OVER (
    PARTITION BY cc.ACADEMIC_YEAR
    ORDER BY STR_TO_DATE(cd.START_DATE, '%Y-%m-%d'),
             COALESCE(so.SECTION_ID, so.SUBJECT_KEY, cc.SUBJECT_ID)
    ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING
  ) AS running_avg_duration_days,
  cc.ACADEMIC_YEAR,
  STR_TO_DATE(cd.START_DATE, '%Y-%m-%d') AS start_date_parsed
FROM subject_offered so
-- prefer course_catalog_subject_offered as primary source of academic year / subject title
JOIN course_catalog_subject_offered cc
  ON so.TERM_CODE = cc.TERM_CODE
  AND so.SUBJECT_ID = cc.SUBJECT_ID
-- map term to time_day to get start/end dates; time_day uses ACADEMIC_TERM_CODE as key in schema
JOIN time_day cd
  ON cc.TERM_CODE = cd.ACADEMIC_TERM_CODE
-- require that meet place maps to a building number; use inner join to exclude missing mappings
JOIN buildings_basic bb
  ON so.MEET_PLACE = bb.BUILDING_NUMBER
WHERE
  cc.ACADEMIC_YEAR IS NOT NULL
  AND cd.START_DATE IS NOT NULL
  AND cd.END_DATE IS NOT NULL
  -- ensure parsed dates are valid-ish (STR_TO_DATE returns NULL if format mismatches)
  AND STR_TO_DATE(cd.START_DATE, '%Y-%m-%d') IS NOT NULL
  AND STR_TO_DATE(cd.END_DATE, '%Y-%m-%d') IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY
  cc.ACADEMIC_YEAR ASC,
  STR_TO_DATE(cd.START_DATE, '%Y-%m-%d') ASC

rows.question: For each course, list its name, name of the building of the course location, the start date, the name of the course before it, and the name of the course after it, access level of the building, and the assignable area of the room used for the course, sorted by the ascending order start date and course name.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH term_start_by_termcode AS (
  SELECT
    at.`TERM_CODE` AS TERM_CODE,
    at.`TERM_START_DATE` AS TERM_START_DATE,
    at.`ACADEMIC_YEAR` AS ACADEMIC_YEAR,
    atp.`TERM_CODE` AS TERM_CODE_from_academic_term_parameter,
    atp.`TERM_START_DATE` AS TERM_START_DATE_from_academic_term_parameter
  FROM academic_terms AS at
  LEFT JOIN academic_term_parameter AS atp
    ON at.`TERM_CODE` = atp.`TERM_CODE`
),
building_by_number AS (
  SELECT
    `BUILDING_NUMBER`,
    `BUILDING_NAME`,
    `BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE`,
    `BUILDING_KEY`
  FROM buildings
),
courses_union AS (
  SELECT
    SUBJECT_TITLE,
    SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE,
    SUBJECT_CODE,
    SUBJECT_NUMBER,
    SUBJECT_ID,
    MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
    TERM_CODE,
    EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE,
    MEET_PLACE
  FROM course_catalog_subject_offered
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    SUBJECT_TITLE,
    SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE,
    SUBJECT_CODE,
    SUBJECT_NUMBER,
    SUBJECT_ID,
    MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
    TERM_CODE,
    EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE,
    MEET_PLACE
  FROM cis_course_catalog
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    SUBJECT_TITLE,
    SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE,
    SUBJECT_CODE,
    SUBJECT_NUMBER,
    SUBJECT_ID,
    MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
    TERM_CODE,
    EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE,
    MEET_PLACE
  FROM drupal_course_catalog
),
courses_with_meta AS (
  SELECT
    c.*,
    COALESCE(c.SUBJECT_TITLE, c.SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE) AS course_name,
    COALESCE(ts.TERM_START_DATE, ts.TERM_START_DATE_from_academic_term_parameter) AS start_date,
    bldg.BUILDING_NAME AS building_name,
    bld.ACCESS_LEVEL_NAME AS building_access_level,
    bldg.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS room_assignable_area
  FROM courses_union AS c
  LEFT JOIN term_start_by_termcode AS ts
    ON ts.TERM_CODE = COALESCE(c.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE, c.TERM_CODE)
  LEFT JOIN building_by_number AS bldg
    ON bldg.BUILDING_NUMBER = c.MEET_PLACE
  LEFT JOIN fclt_building AS bld
    ON bld.BUILDING_KEY = bldg.BUILDING_KEY
)
SELECT
  course_name,
  building_name,
  start_date,
  LAG(course_name) OVER (
    PARTITION BY COALESCE(SUBJECT_ID, MASTER_SUBJECT_ID)
    ORDER BY
      COALESCE(NULLIF(CAST(SUBJECT_NUMBER AS SIGNED), 0), 0),
      course_name
  ) AS previous_course,
  LEAD(course_name) OVER (
    PARTITION BY COALESCE(SUBJECT_ID, MASTER_SUBJECT_ID)
    ORDER BY
      COALESCE(NULLIF(CAST(SUBJECT_NUMBER AS SIGNED), 0), 0),
      course_name
  ) AS next_course,
  building_access_level,
  room_assignable_area
FROM courses_with_meta
ORDER BY
  STR_TO_DATE(start_date, '%Y-%m-%d') ASC,
  course_name ASC

rows.question: For email lists with names starting with e (case insensitive), containing 10 to 20 members inclusive, and where over 75% are computer science students, provide the list name, owner, and member count.
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT
  m.MOIRA_LIST_NAME AS list_name,
  o.OWNER AS owner,
  cnt.member_count AS member_count
FROM moira_list m
JOIN moira_list_owner o
  ON m.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = o.MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY
JOIN (
  SELECT
    d.MOIRA_LIST_KEY,
    COUNT(*) AS member_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN s.DEPARTMENT = '6' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cs_count
  FROM moira_list_detail d
  LEFT JOIN mit_student_directory s
    ON d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID = s.MIT_ID
       OR d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID = s.EMAIL_ADDRESS
       OR d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER = s.EMAIL_ADDRESS
       OR d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER = s.FULL_NAME
       OR d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER = s.FULL_NAME_UPPERCASE
  GROUP BY d.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
) cnt
  ON m.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = cnt.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
WHERE
  m.IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST = '1'
  AND LOWER(m.MOIRA_LIST_NAME) LIKE 'e%'
  AND cnt.member_count BETWEEN 10 AND 20
  AND (cnt.cs_count / GREATEST(cnt.member_count,1)) > 0.75

rows.question: For students with last names starting with K, list their names, the phone numbers of departments they belong to, total number of mailing lists each student is in, and the average size of the mailing lists each student is in.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH departments_contact AS (
  SELECT
    `HR_ORG_UNIT_ID` AS HR_ORG_UNIT_ID,
    `HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE` AS HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE,
    `OFFICE_PHONE` AS OFFICE_PHONE,
    `OFFICE_LOCATION` AS OFFICE_LOCATION
  FROM `drupal_employee_directory`
  GROUP BY
    `HR_ORG_UNIT_ID`,
    `HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE`,
    `OFFICE_PHONE`,
    `OFFICE_LOCATION`
),
sis_persons_basic AS (
  -- use mit_student_directory as the SIS student source when available; fall back to employee-like directory if needed
  SELECT
    msd.FULL_NAME AS FULL_NAME,
    msd.FIRST_NAME AS FIRST_NAME,
    msd.LAST_NAME AS LAST_NAME,
    msd.EMAIL_ADDRESS AS EMAIL_ADDRESS,
    msd.DEPARTMENT AS DEPARTMENT,
    msd.OFFICE_PHONE AS OFFICE_PHONE
  FROM `mit_student_directory` msd
),
-- compute each moira list's size (distinct members)
moira_list_sizes AS (
  SELECT
    MOIRA_LIST_KEY,
    COUNT(DISTINCT MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID) AS list_size
  FROM `moira_list_detail`
  GROUP BY MOIRA_LIST_KEY
),
-- for each student, get distinct lists they belong to and aggregate count + average list size
student_moira_agg AS (
  SELECT
    md.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID AS MIT_ID,
    COUNT(DISTINCT md.MOIRA_LIST_KEY) AS mailing_list_count,
    AVG(mls.list_size) AS average_mailing_list_size
  FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID, MOIRA_LIST_KEY
    FROM `moira_list_detail`
  ) md
  LEFT JOIN moira_list_sizes mls
    ON md.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = mls.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
  GROUP BY md.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID
)
SELECT
  spb.FULL_NAME AS student_full_name,
  -- attempt to get department phone: look up department code in sis_admin_department then fallback to student's OFFICE_PHONE
  COALESCE(sad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER, dc.OFFICE_PHONE, spb.OFFICE_PHONE) AS department_phone,
  COALESCE(sma.mailing_list_count, 0) AS mailing_list_count,
  sma.average_mailing_list_size AS avg_mailing_list_size
FROM sis_persons_basic spb
LEFT JOIN `sis_department` sd
  ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = spb.DEPARTMENT
LEFT JOIN `sis_admin_department` sad
  ON sad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE = sd.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE
LEFT JOIN departments_contact dc
  ON dc.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID = sd.DLC_KEY -- best-effort join to department contact; keys vary in schema so this is a non-restrictive attempt
LEFT JOIN student_moira_agg sma
  ON sma.MIT_ID = spb.FULL_NAME /* no direct MIT_ID in mit_student_directory; if MIT_ID exists adjust join to student identifier */
WHERE spb.LAST_NAME LIKE 'K%'
ORDER BY spb.LAST_NAME ASC, spb.FIRST_NAME ASC

rows.question: From the 100 email lists with the most number of subscribers, list their names, their total number of subscribers, their public status, the name of the department with the most presence in the list, and the number of students from this department in the list.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH mailing_list_members_normalized AS (
  SELECT
    ml.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` AS list_id,
    ml.`MOIRA_LIST_NAME` AS list_name,
    mld.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID` AS member_id,
    ml.`IS_PUBLIC` AS is_public,
    ml.`IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST` AS is_moira_mailing_list
  FROM `moira_list` ml
  JOIN `moira_list_detail` mld
    ON ml.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` = mld.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY`
  WHERE ml.`IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST` = 'Y'
),
list_totals AS (
  -- compute total subscribers per list (count distinct member MIT_ID where available,
  -- otherwise count rows)
  SELECT
    list_id,
    list_name,
    COUNT(*) AS total_subscribers,
    -- if IS_PUBLIC is consistent per list, MAX will return that value; otherwise returns a non-null if any
    CASE
      WHEN MAX(is_public) IS NULL THEN NULL
      ELSE MAX(is_public)
    END AS is_public
  FROM mailing_list_members_normalized
  GROUP BY list_id, list_name
),
-- student affiliation: join member MIT_ID to se_person (SIS) to identify students.
-- The schema does not provide an explicit student flag; we treat rows present in se_person as SIS-affiliated.
student_members AS (
  SELECT
    m.list_id,
    m.member_id,
    sp.MIT_ID AS sis_mit_id,
    sp.ORGANIZATION AS sis_department_code
  FROM mailing_list_members_normalized m
  JOIN se_person sp
    ON sp.MIT_ID = m.member_id
  WHERE m.member_id IS NOT NULL
),
-- map SIS department code to department name from student_department
student_dept_mapped AS (
  SELECT
    sm.list_id,
    sm.member_id,
    sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS department_name
  FROM student_members sm
  LEFT JOIN student_department sd
    ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sm.sis_department_code
),
-- count distinct student members per list per department
dept_counts AS (
  SELECT
    list_id,
    department_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT member_id) AS student_count
  FROM student_dept_mapped
  GROUP BY list_id, department_name
),
-- pick top department per list, tie-breaker: lexicographically smallest department_name
dept_ranks AS (
  SELECT
    dc.list_id,
    dc.department_name,
    dc.student_count,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY dc.list_id
      ORDER BY dc.student_count DESC,
               -- NULLs last so that real names win over NULL; to ensure deterministic tie-breaker:
               CASE WHEN dc.department_name IS NULL THEN 'ZZZZZZZZ' ELSE dc.department_name END ASC
    ) AS rn
  FROM dept_counts dc
)
SELECT
  lt.list_name AS list_name,
  lt.total_subscribers AS total_subscribers,
  -- normalize public flag to NULL/'public'/'private' for clarity
  CASE
    WHEN lt.is_public IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN UPPER(lt.is_public) IN ('Y','T','TRUE','1') THEN 'public'
    WHEN UPPER(lt.is_public) IN ('N','F','FALSE','0') THEN 'private'
    ELSE lt.is_public
  END AS is_public,
  dr.department_name AS top_department_name,
  COALESCE(dr.student_count, 0) AS top_department_student_count
FROM list_totals lt
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT list_id, department_name, student_count
  FROM dept_ranks
  WHERE rn = 1
) dr
  ON dr.list_id = lt.list_id
ORDER BY lt.total_subscribers DESC
LIMIT 100

rows.question: Calculate the total assignable and non-assignable area for each building by summing up the respective areas of all its floors. For each building, list the building name, building number, total assignable area, total non-assignable area, and total room count, sorted in descending order of the total assignable area.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH building_floor_summary AS (
  SELECT
    b.BUILDING_KEY,
    ff.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY,
    COALESCE(ff.ASSIGNABLE_AREA, 0) AS floor_assignable_area,
    COALESCE(ff.NON_ASSIGNABLE_AREA, 0) AS floor_non_assignable_area
  FROM buildings b
  LEFT JOIN fclt_building fb
    ON fb.BUILDING_NUMBER = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
  LEFT JOIN fclt_floor ff
    ON ff.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY
),
building_room_counts AS (
  SELECT
    BUILDING_KEY,
    COALESCE(COUNT(DISTINCT ROOM), 0) AS room_count
  FROM fac_rooms
  WHERE BUILDING_KEY IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY BUILDING_KEY
),
building_aggregates AS (
  SELECT
    bfs.BUILDING_KEY,
    SUM(bfs.floor_assignable_area) AS total_assignable,
    SUM(bfs.floor_non_assignable_area) AS total_non_assignable
  FROM building_floor_summary bfs
  GROUP BY bfs.BUILDING_KEY
)
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  COALESCE(ba.total_assignable, 0) AS TOTAL_ASSIGNABLE_AREA,
  COALESCE(ba.total_non_assignable, 0) AS TOTAL_NON_ASSIGNABLE_AREA,
  COALESCE(brc.room_count, 0) AS TOTAL_ROOM_COUNT
FROM buildings b
LEFT JOIN building_aggregates ba
  ON ba.BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY
LEFT JOIN building_room_counts brc
  ON brc.BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY
ORDER BY TOTAL_ASSIGNABLE_AREA DESC

rows.question: List all rooms in building 45, including their full name, area, major use, the organization that occupies them, the count of rooms per major use, and the total area occupied by rooms for each organization.

  fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME AS OCCUPYING_ORGANIZATION,
  COALESCE(mu.MAJOR_USE_ROOM_COUNT, 0) AS MAJOR_USE_ROOM_COUNT,

rows.question: List the name, number, construction date, and type of all buildings, along with the count of addresses associated with each building, the average gross area of the buildings, and the total number of rooms in each building. Sort the results by building name.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH buildings_gross_sqft_stats AS (
  SELECT
    b.BUILDING_KEY,
    (SELECT AVG(bb.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE) FROM buildings bb) AS AVG_BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE
  FROM buildings b
),
buildings_address_counts AS (
  SELECT
    b.BUILDING_KEY,
    (
      (CASE WHEN b.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(b.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS) <> '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
      +
      (CASE WHEN b.BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(b.BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS) <> '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
    ) AS ADDRESS_COUNT
  FROM buildings b
)
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  NULL AS CONSTRUCTION_DATE, /* no construction date column in schema; per rules use NULL */
  NULL AS BUILDING_TYPE,     /* no BUILDING_TYPE column in buildings; per rules use NULL */
  COALESCE(a.ADDRESS_COUNT, 0) AS ADDRESS_COUNT,
  g.AVG_BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS AVG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  COALESCE(b.BUILDING_COUNTER, 0) AS TOTAL_ROOM_COUNT
FROM buildings b
LEFT JOIN buildings_address_counts a
  ON b.BUILDING_KEY = a.BUILDING_KEY
LEFT JOIN buildings_gross_sqft_stats g
  ON b.BUILDING_KEY = g.BUILDING_KEY
ORDER BY b.BUILDING_NAME ASC

rows.question: For each department, list its name, number of unique courses offered, the number of unique reserved materials, and the number of unique instructors associated with those courses, sorted by the number of unique courses offered in descending order.
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT
  dept.department_name,
  dept.department_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT dept.course_key) AS unique_courses_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT dept.library_subject_offered_key) AS unique_reserved_materials_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME) AS unique_instructors_count
FROM (
  -- unify departmental rows from subject_offered, library_subject_offered, course_catalog_subject_offered, drupal_course_catalog
  SELECT
    OFFER_DEPT_CODE AS department_id,
    OFFER_DEPT_NAME AS department_name,
    MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER AS course_key,
    NULL AS library_subject_offered_key
  FROM subject_offered
  WHERE OFFER_DEPT_CODE IS NOT NULL

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    OFFER_DEPT_CODE AS department_id,
    OFFER_DEPT_NAME AS department_name,
    MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER AS course_key,
    LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY AS library_subject_offered_key
  FROM library_subject_offered
  WHERE OFFER_DEPT_CODE IS NOT NULL

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    DEPARTMENT_CODE AS department_id,
    DEPARTMENT_NAME AS department_name,
    CONCAT(COALESCE(SUBJECT_CODE,''), '-', COALESCE(SUBJECT_NUMBER,'')) AS course_key,
    NULL AS library_subject_offered_key
  FROM course_catalog_subject_offered
  WHERE DEPARTMENT_CODE IS NOT NULL

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    DEPARTMENT_CODE AS department_id,
    DEPARTMENT_NAME AS department_name,
    CONCAT(COALESCE(SUBJECT_CODE,''), '-', COALESCE(SUBJECT_NUMBER,'')) AS course_key,
    NULL AS library_subject_offered_key
  FROM drupal_course_catalog
  WHERE DEPARTMENT_CODE IS NOT NULL
) AS dept
LEFT JOIN library_course_instructor lci
  ON lci.DEPARTMENT = dept.department_name
GROUP BY
  dept.department_name,
  dept.department_id
ORDER BY
  unique_courses_count DESC

rows.question: For each course title, list the title, the total number of reserved materials, and the count of distinct material status associated with those materials, sorted by the total number of reserved materials in descending order.
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(NULLIF(cso.SUBJECT_TITLE, ''), NULLIF(cso.SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE, ''), cso.PRINT_SUBJECT_ID) AS COURSE_TITLE,
  COUNT(lr.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY) AS TOTAL_RESERVED_MATERIALS,
  COUNT(DISTINCT lms.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS) AS DISTINCT_MATERIAL_STATUS_COUNT
FROM library_reserve_matrl_detail lrm
-- join to reserve catalog to get each reserved material record (one row per catalog entry)
LEFT JOIN library_reserve_catalog lr
  ON lrm.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY = lr.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY
-- join to material status to get the status label (exclude NULL statuses from distinct count by using LEFT JOIN but DISTINCT will ignore NULL)
LEFT JOIN library_material_status lms
  ON lrm.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = lms.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY
-- join to a course/title source: prefer SUBJECT_TITLE from course_catalog_subject_offered; fall back to SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE or PRINT_SUBJECT_ID
LEFT JOIN course_catalog_subject_offered cso
  ON lrm.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = cso.SECTION_ID
    OR lrm.SUBJECT_ID = cso.SUBJECT_ID
    OR lrm.TERM_CODE = cso.TERM_CODE
WHERE
  -- only include rows with a non-null course title per requirements
  COALESCE(NULLIF(cso.SUBJECT_TITLE, ''), NULLIF(cso.SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE, ''), cso.PRINT_SUBJECT_ID) IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  COALESCE(NULLIF(cso.SUBJECT_TITLE, ''), NULLIF(cso.SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE, ''), cso.PRINT_SUBJECT_ID)
ORDER BY
  TOTAL_RESERVED_MATERIALS DESC

rows.question: For each instructor, list their name, the number of unique courses they teach, the total number of material assignments, average publication year, and number of distinct status, sorted by the number of unique courses in descending order.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH catalog_instructor_sections AS (
  SELECT
    SECTION_ID,
    RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME,
    SUBJECT_CODE,
    SUBJECT_NUMBER,
    SUBJECT_ID,
    MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
    -- carry keys for joinability
    TERM_CODE,
    EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE,
    DEPARTMENT_CODE
  FROM course_catalog_subject_offered
  WHERE RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME IS NOT NULL
    AND RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME <> ''
),
materials_by_course AS (
  -- Build a course_key for each material assignment that matches the logic used for courses:
  -- prefer SUBJECT_ID, otherwise SUBJECT_CODE-SUBJECT_NUMBER, otherwise TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
  SELECT
    td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY,
    td.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY,
    td.SUBJECT_ID AS td_subject_id,
    -- normalized course key
    COALESCE(
      NULLIF(td.SUBJECT_ID, ''),
      NULLIF(CONCAT(NULLIF(sc.SUBJECT_CODE, ''), '-', NULLIF(sc.SUBJECT_NUMBER, '')), ''),
      NULLIF(td.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY, '')
    ) AS course_key,
    -- treat RECORD_COUNT as number of assignments (default 1)
    COALESCE(SUM(COALESCE(td.RECORD_COUNT, 1)), 0) AS assignments,
    -- publication year normalized to integer when numeric, NULL otherwise
    CASE WHEN tm.`YEAR` REGEXP '^[0-9]+$' THEN CAST(tm.`YEAR` AS SIGNED) ELSE NULL END AS pub_year,
    tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS AS status
  FROM tip_detail td
  LEFT JOIN tip_material tm ON td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY = tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY
  LEFT JOIN tip_material_status tms ON td.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY
  -- try to get SUBJECT_CODE/SUBJECT_NUMBER for building a code-number key when SUBJECT_ID absent
  LEFT JOIN course_catalog_subject_offered sc ON td.SUBJECT_ID = sc.SUBJECT_ID
  GROUP BY course_key, td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY, pub_year, status, td.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY, td.SUBJECT_ID
)
SELECT
  cis.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME AS instructor_name,
  -- count distinct courses per instructor using the same uniqueness rules:
  COUNT(DISTINCT
    COALESCE(
      NULLIF(cis.SUBJECT_ID, ''),
      NULLIF(CONCAT(NULLIF(cis.SUBJECT_CODE, ''), '-', NULLIF(cis.SUBJECT_NUMBER, '')), ''),
      NULLIF(cis.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, ''),
      NULLIF(cis.SECTION_ID, '')
    )
  ) AS unique_course_count,
  -- total material assignment records linked to the instructor's courses
  COALESCE(SUM(m.assignments), 0) AS total_material_assignments,
  -- average publication year across material assignments linked to the instructor's courses.
  -- exclude NULL pub_year values so AVG returns NULL when none present.
  AVG(m.pub_year) AS average_publication_year,
  -- distinct count of status values among those material assignments
  COALESCE(COUNT(DISTINCT m.status), 0) AS distinct_status_count
FROM catalog_instructor_sections cis
LEFT JOIN materials_by_course m
  ON (
       -- match by SUBJECT_ID if present
       (cis.SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL AND cis.SUBJECT_ID <> '' AND cis.SUBJECT_ID = m.course_key)
    OR -- match by SUBJECT_CODE-SUBJECT_NUMBER if present
       (cis.SUBJECT_CODE IS NOT NULL AND cis.SUBJECT_CODE <> ''
        AND cis.SUBJECT_NUMBER IS NOT NULL AND cis.SUBJECT_NUMBER <> ''
        AND CONCAT(cis.SUBJECT_CODE, '-', cis.SUBJECT_NUMBER) = m.course_key)
    OR -- match by MASTER_SUBJECT_ID when material course_key equals that (fallback)
       (cis.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL AND cis.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID <> '' AND cis.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID = m.course_key)
    OR -- last fallback: match TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY to section's SECTION_ID (if data uses that)
       (m.course_key = m.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY AND cis.SECTION_ID IS NOT NULL AND cis.SECTION_ID <> '' AND cis.SECTION_ID = m.course_key)
  )
GROUP BY cis.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT
    COALESCE(
      NULLIF(cis.SUBJECT_ID, ''),
      NULLIF(CONCAT(NULLIF(cis.SUBJECT_CODE, ''), '-', NULLIF(cis.SUBJECT_NUMBER, '')), ''),
      NULLIF(cis.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, ''),
      NULLIF(cis.SECTION_ID, '')
    )
  ) > 0
ORDER BY unique_course_count DESC

rows.question: For each publication year, list the year, the total number of reserved materials, the average length of their titles, distinct number of status, and number of courses, sorted by publication year in descending order.
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT
  ACADEMIC_YEAR AS publication_year,
  COUNT(*) AS total_reserved_materials,
  AVG(CHAR_LENGTH(NULLIF(SUBJECT_TITLE, ''))) AS avg_title_length,
  COUNT(DISTINCT NULLIF(HASS_ATTRIBUTE, '')) AS distinct_status_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT NULLIF(SECTION_ID, COALESCE(NULLIF(SECTION_ID, ''), SUBJECT_ID))) AS distinct_course_count
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered
-- Filter: treat "reserved materials" as records present in the reserve catalog context.
-- The schema does not have an explicit "reserved" flag in course_catalog_subject_offered,
-- so use the library_reserve_catalog linkage via library_reserve_matrl_detail if present.
-- Join to library_reserve_matrl_detail to restrict to actually reserved material records.
WHERE ACADEMIC_YEAR IS NOT NULL
  AND ACADEMIC_YEAR <> ''
  -- Exclude rows with NULL titles when computing average (NULL title lengths ignored by AVG due to NULL)
  -- Keep rows regardless of SUBJECT_TITLE NULL for counts; AVG uses NULLIF above to turn '' into NULL.
  AND EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM library_reserve_matrl_detail l
    WHERE l.TERM_CODE = course_catalog_subject_offered.TERM_CODE
      AND l.SUBJECT_ID = course_catalog_subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID
  )
GROUP BY ACADEMIC_YEAR
ORDER BY ACADEMIC_YEAR DESC

rows.question: For each IAP category, list the category name, the sponsor name, the number of activities offered, and the average fee per activity, sorted by the number of activities in descending order.
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(c.HASS_ATTRIBUTE_DESC, 'Uncategorized') AS CATEGORY_NAME,
  COALESCE(fd.FULL_NAME, c.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME, 'Unknown') AS SPONSOR_NAME,
  COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(c.SECTION_ID, c.SUBJECT_ID)) AS ACTIVITY_COUNT,
  -- average only over numeric, non-null, non-zero fees per instructions (zero treated as a numeric value; question said include only numeric fee values and ignore non-numeric; original used NULLIF(...,0) so zeros ignored)
  -- compute average of fees from iap_subject_detail joined rows; if no numeric fees for category result will be NULL
  ROUND(
    AVG(tp.fee_num),
    2
  ) AS AVG_FEE_PER_ACTIVITY
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered c
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY AS SECTION_ID,
    TERM_CODE,
    -- try to coerce FEE to numeric; include only rows where FEE is not null and is numeric
    CAST(FEE AS DECIMAL(18,2)) AS fee_num
  FROM iap_subject_detail
  WHERE FEE IS NOT NULL
    -- exclude values that cannot be cast to numeric by filtering using a simple numeric pattern
    AND FEE REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$'
) tp
  ON (
       (c.SECTION_ID IS NOT NULL AND c.SECTION_ID = tp.SECTION_ID)
       OR (c.SECTION_ID IS NULL AND c.SUBJECT_ID = tp.SECTION_ID)
     )
LEFT JOIN drupal_employee_directory fd
  ON fd.FULL_NAME = c.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME
WHERE
  -- include only activities offered in IAP (flag in course_catalog_subject_offered) or that have an iap_subject_detail record (tp) — per requirements exclude non-IAP activities
  (c.IS_OFFERED_IAP = 'Y' OR tp.fee_num IS NOT NULL)
GROUP BY
  COALESCE(c.HASS_ATTRIBUTE_DESC, 'Uncategorized'),
  COALESCE(fd.FULL_NAME, c.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME, 'Unknown')
ORDER BY
  ACTIVITY_COUNT DESC

rows.question: For each sponsor, list the sponsor name, the number of IAP sessions hosted, and the number of unique subjects organized.

rows.question: For each person role and IAP category, list the role, the category name, the number of people in this role, and the average fee, sorted by the role count in descending order.
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT
  isp.PERSON_ROLE AS role,
  ic.IAP_CATEGORY_NAME AS category_name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT isp.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY) AS number_of_people,
  AVG(
    CASE
      WHEN TRIM(COALESCE(isd.FEE, '')) = '' THEN NULL
      WHEN isd.FEE REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$' THEN CAST(isd.FEE AS DECIMAL(18,2))
      ELSE NULL
    END

FROM iap_subject_detail AS isd

  ON isd.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY = isp.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY
JOIN iap_subject_category AS ic
  ON isd.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY = ic.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY

  AND TRIM(COALESCE(ic.IAP_CATEGORY_NAME, '')) <> ''
GROUP BY isp.PERSON_ROLE, ic.IAP_CATEGORY_NAME

rows.question: List the names of the buildings with the most floors. If there are ties, list each one separately.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH buildings_rowlevel AS (
  SELECT
    `BUILDING_KEY`,
    `BUILDING_NAME`,
    -- normalize BUILDING_COUNTER to integer, treat non-numeric/empty as NULL
    CASE
      WHEN `BUILDING_COUNTER` IS NULL THEN NULL
      WHEN TRIM(`BUILDING_COUNTER`) = '' THEN NULL
      WHEN `BUILDING_COUNTER` REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+$' THEN CAST(`BUILDING_COUNTER` AS SIGNED)
      WHEN `BUILDING_COUNTER` REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+$' THEN CAST(FLOOR(CAST(`BUILDING_COUNTER` AS DECIMAL(30,10))) AS SIGNED)
      ELSE NULL
    END AS BUILDING_COUNTER
  FROM `buildings`
  -- keep only rows from this table and ensure there's a key present
  WHERE `BUILDING_KEY` IS NOT NULL
),
max_counter AS (
  SELECT MAX(BUILDING_COUNTER) AS max_building_counter
  FROM buildings_rowlevel
  WHERE BUILDING_COUNTER IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  b.BUILDING_COUNTER AS BUILDING_COUNTER
FROM buildings_rowlevel b
JOIN max_counter m ON b.BUILDING_COUNTER = m.max_building_counter
WHERE b.BUILDING_COUNTER IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY b.BUILDING_NAME ASC

rows.question: For subjects offered in the summer term, list the subject titles, number of instructors, and the length of the longest instructor name.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH source_drupal AS (
  SELECT
    EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
    SUBJECT_ID,
    SUBJECT_TITLE,
    FALL_INSTRUCTORS,
    SPRING_INSTRUCTORS
  FROM drupal_course_catalog
),
source_cis AS (
  SELECT
    EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
    SUBJECT_ID,
    SUBJECT_TITLE,
    FALL_INSTRUCTORS,
    SPRING_INSTRUCTORS
  FROM cis_course_catalog
),
nums AS (
  SELECT 1 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL
  SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL
  SELECT 9 UNION ALL SELECT 10
),
-- expand comma-separated instructor lists for rows whose TERM_CODE indicates summer
expanded_instructors AS (
  -- drupal fall instructors (included if row is a summer TERM_CODE)
  SELECT
    s.TERM_CODE,
    s.SUBJECT_ID,
    s.SUBJECT_TITLE,
    TRIM(SUBSTRING_INDEX(SUBSTRING_INDEX(s.FALL_INSTRUCTORS, ',', n.n), ',', -1)) AS instructor_name
  FROM source_drupal s
  JOIN nums n ON s.FALL_INSTRUCTORS IS NOT NULL AND s.FALL_INSTRUCTORS <> ''
  WHERE s.TERM_CODE LIKE '%SU'
  UNION ALL
  -- drupal spring instructors (sometimes data may be populated for summer rows)
  SELECT
    s.TERM_CODE,
    s.SUBJECT_ID,
    s.SUBJECT_TITLE,
    TRIM(SUBSTRING_INDEX(SUBSTRING_INDEX(s.SPRING_INSTRUCTORS, ',', n.n), ',', -1)) AS instructor_name
  FROM source_drupal s
  JOIN nums n ON s.SPRING_INSTRUCTORS IS NOT NULL AND s.SPRING_INSTRUCTORS <> ''
  WHERE s.TERM_CODE LIKE '%SU'
  UNION ALL
  -- cis fall instructors
  SELECT
    s.TERM_CODE,
    s.SUBJECT_ID,
    s.SUBJECT_TITLE,
    TRIM(SUBSTRING_INDEX(SUBSTRING_INDEX(s.FALL_INSTRUCTORS, ',', n.n), ',', -1)) AS instructor_name
  FROM source_cis s
  JOIN nums n ON s.FALL_INSTRUCTORS IS NOT NULL AND s.FALL_INSTRUCTORS <> ''
  WHERE s.TERM_CODE LIKE '%SU'
  UNION ALL
  -- cis spring instructors
  SELECT
    s.TERM_CODE,
    s.SUBJECT_ID,
    s.SUBJECT_TITLE,
    TRIM(SUBSTRING_INDEX(SUBSTRING_INDEX(s.SPRING_INSTRUCTORS, ',', n.n), ',', -1)) AS instructor_name
  FROM source_cis s
  JOIN nums n ON s.SPRING_INSTRUCTORS IS NOT NULL AND s.SPRING_INSTRUCTORS <> ''
  WHERE s.TERM_CODE LIKE '%SU'
),
-- unioned and cleaned instructor rows
clean_instructors AS (
  SELECT
    TERM_CODE,
    SUBJECT_ID,
    SUBJECT_TITLE,
    instructor_name
  FROM expanded_instructors
  WHERE instructor_name IS NOT NULL AND instructor_name <> ''
)
SELECT
  SUBJECT_TITLE AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  COUNT(DISTINCT instructor_name) AS INSTRUCTOR_COUNT,
  MAX(CHAR_LENGTH(instructor_name)) AS MAX_INSTRUCTOR_NAME_LENGTH
FROM clean_instructors
GROUP BY SUBJECT_TITLE, TERM_CODE
ORDER BY SUBJECT_TITLE

rows.question: For each school, list the school name, total number of courses that appear in SIS subject code catalog, and the total number of degree-granting courses that appear in SIS subject code catalog.

WITH sis_course_catalog_rows AS (
  SELECT

rows.question: For each department, list the department name, department phone number, number of students, and the length of the longest student full name in that department.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH students_core_names AS (
SELECT
  `drupal_employee_directory`.`MIT_ID` AS `MIT_ID`,
  `drupal_employee_directory`.`FIRST_NAME` AS `FIRST_NAME`,
  `drupal_employee_directory`.`MIDDLE_NAME` AS `MIDDLE_NAME`,
  `drupal_employee_directory`.`LAST_NAME` AS `LAST_NAME`,
  `drupal_employee_directory`.`FULL_NAME` AS `FULL_NAME`
FROM `drupal_employee_directory`
),
course_subjects_catalog AS (
SELECT
  `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_CODE` AS `SUBJECT_CODE`,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` AS `DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS `DEPARTMENT_NAME`
FROM
  `cis_course_catalog`
GROUP BY
  `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID`,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_CODE`,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`
),
departments_directory_basic AS (
SELECT
  dmd.MIT_ID                AS MIT_ID,
  dmd.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID        AS HR_ORG_UNIT_ID,
  dmd.HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE     AS HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(dmd.OFFICE_PHONE, ''), 'NULL') AS OFFICE_PHONE
FROM
  drupal_employee_directory dmd
)
SELECT
  d.HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE AS department_name,
  d.OFFICE_PHONE AS department_phone,
  COALESCE(s.num_students, 0) AS number_of_students,
  COALESCE(s.longest_name_length, 0) AS longest_student_full_name_length
FROM departments_directory_basic d
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    sd.MIT_ID, -- carry key though not returned; used to join to dept mapping
    dept.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID AS HR_ORG_UNIT_ID,
    COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY dept.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID) AS num_students,
    MAX(LENGTH(
      CASE
        WHEN COALESCE(sd.FULL_NAME, '') <> '' THEN sd.FULL_NAME
        ELSE TRIM(CONCAT(
          COALESCE(sd.FIRST_NAME, ''),
          IF(sd.MIDDLE_NAME IS NOT NULL AND sd.MIDDLE_NAME <> '', CONCAT(' ', sd.MIDDLE_NAME), ''),
          IF(sd.LAST_NAME IS NOT NULL AND sd.LAST_NAME <> '', CONCAT(' ', sd.LAST_NAME), '')
        ))
      END
    )) OVER (PARTITION BY dept.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID) AS longest_name_length
  FROM students_core_names sd
  JOIN departments_directory_basic dept
    ON sd.MIT_ID = dept.MIT_ID
) s
  ON d.HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE = d.HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE AND s.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID = d.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID
GROUP BY
  d.HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE,
  d.OFFICE_PHONE,
  s.num_students,
  s.longest_name_length
